Congressman Ernix Dionisio of the 1st District of Manila expresses his heartfelt gratitude to President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. for his compassionate and prompt response in supporting families affected by the devastating fire in Happyland, Barangay 105, Tondo, Manila, on September 13, 2025.

During his visit to the affected area on Thursday, President Marcos personally oversaw the distribution of aid from the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) at temporary shelters in Gen. Vicente Lim Elementary School and Antonio Villegas Vocational High School. His assurance that the government will stand by the victims until they regain normalcy brought hope to the community. “Kahit na ganito ang nangyari, asahan po ninyo ang gobyerno ninyo ay nandito, binabantayan kayo, inaalalayan kayo, at titiyakin namin na maaalagaan namin kayo sa lahat ng inyong pangangailangan,” President Marcos told the evacuees, adding, “Kaunting tiyaga lang po, gagawin po natin ang lahat para makabalik na kayo sa normal na ninyong buhay.”

“I am deeply thankful to President Marcos for his immediate action and unwavering commitment to the people of Happyland,” said Congressman Dionisio. “Ang kanyang pamumuno sa pagpapakilos ng mga tulong, tulad ng food packs, hygiene kits, at cash assistance, ay nagpapakita ng tunay na malasakit sa mga nangangailangan.”

#younggunsph #PBBM #BagongPilipinas #20thCongress #KayErnixTayo

Nakatakdang isagawa ang "Baha Sa Luneta" at “Trillion Peso March” rally sa magkaibang bahagi ng bansa sa Linggo, Setyembre 21, bilang pagkondena sa korapsyon sa flood control projects.

Gaganapin ang “Baha sa Luneta: Aksyon na Laban sa Korapsyon” o “Billion People March” sa Luneta Park, Maynila mula alas-9 ng umaga sa nasabing araw.

Ito ay inorganisa ng mga student at youth leaders kabilang ang Taumbayan Ayaw sa Magnanakaw at Abusado Network Alliance, na isang grupo ng mga paaralan sa Taft Avenue; youth environmentalist na Panatang Luntian Coalition; at iba pang student council mula sa iba't ibang unibersidad.

Gaganapin naman ang “Trillion Peso March" sa EDSA People Power Monument sa Quezon City mula alas-2 ng hapon sa Linggo.

Ito naman ay inorganisa ng mga Catholic at Protestant leaders sa ilalim ng Church Leaders Council for National Transformation (CLCNT), 1Sambayan, at iba pang civil society organizations.

NCR-PRSD Launches Final Leg of Rain Ready Caravan for Central Luzon
 
DOST-PAGASA through the NCR-PRSD, together with the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) Region 3, concluded the final leg of the Rain Ready Caravan 2025: Handa sa Ulan, Handa sa Baha in Central Luzon, completing a three-day regional series that earlier covered CALABARZON and Metro Manila. The event gathered more than 100 Zoom participants and nearly 100 Facebook Live viewers, including LGU representatives, DRRM officers, educators, media, and stakeholders from Zambales, Bataan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bulacan, Nueva Ecija, and Aurora — all united in strengthening resilience against floods and heavy rainfall.
 
In his opening message, Engr. Lorenzo A. Moron, PAGASA-NCR Chief, emphasized Central Luzon’s exposure to an average of five tropical cyclones annually, a major threat to agriculture and vulnerable communities. He urged a shift from reactive response to proactive preparedness anchored on science, particularly PAGASA’s Rainfall Warning System and Impact-Based Forecasting. “Disaster preparedness is not about fear, but about confidence through knowledge, planning, and collective action,” he said.

PAGASA Administrator Dr. Nathaniel T. Servando, in his keynote, highlighted the caravan’s timeliness amid Tropical Cyclone Nando and the looming La Niña, which is expected to bring above-normal rainfall. He reminded participants that forecasts must guide decisions and not just deliver alerts, stressing that “resilience is a shared responsibility” that requires stronger connections between science, policy, and communities.

OCD Region 3 Director Amador V. Corpus further reinforced the four pillars of DRRM — prevention, preparedness, response, and recovery — and cited practical steps such as preparing go-bags, mapping evacuation routes, conducting drills, and ensuring readiness at the barangay level, declaring that “preparedness is not the duty of a few — it is everyone’s responsibility.”
The technical sessions provided deeper insight into PAGASA and OCD’s tools and approaches. Mr. Renier Agas, Weather Specialist I, discussed the Thunderstorm and Rainfall Warning System, developed after Tropical Storm Ondoy in 2009, and explained how warnings are generated, validated, and disseminated to the public. He stressed that technology only saves lives when paired with awareness and coordinated local action, citing real cases where timely alerts reduced losses and casualties.
Ms. Julie M. Nimes, Weather Specialist II, then introduced the Impact-Based Forecasting and Warning System, which predicts not just the weather but its consequences such as casualties, evacuations, and economic disruption. Developed with the UK Met Office and WMO, this system proved effective during Super Typhoon Carina in 2024 and is now set to expand in Central Luzon, with PAGASA establishing a dedicated regional group chat for real-time coordination.
Closing the technical sessions, Ms. Shelby A. Ruiz, Chief of DRRM Division, OCD Region 3, explained how early warning systems are operationalized under the NDRRMOC SOPG 2024. She described EWS as a people-centered process — from risk monitoring to timely, accessible warning dissemination that triggers action. Highlighting platforms like PAGASA advisories, Flood Information Bulletins, and the DRRM Unified System Interface, she stressed that warnings must be tailored to barangays, schools, responders, and the public — and reinforced by drills, evacuation plans, and feedback loops. “The goal is not just to warn — but to ensure warnings lead to life-saving action and lasting resilience,” she affirmed.
In his closing remarks, Dr. Marcelino Q. Villafuerte, DOST-PAGASA Deputy Administrator for R&D, thanked all participants and partners, noting the event’s timeliness amid Tropical Depression Mirasol and Tropical Storm Nando. “This caravan is not just educational — it is essential,” he said, praising the PAGASA-OCD collaboration and urging swift adoption of IBF across Central Luzon. “Through science, partnership, and action — we can turn warnings into protection.”
Hosted by Aira DG. Bernardino, the event ended not as a finale, but as a launchpad — marking the start of institutionalized, community-driven, science-backed weather readiness across Central Luzon. As climate risks grow more severe and rainfall more unpredictable, the Rain Ready Caravan empowers every household, barangay, and province to face the rain — not with fear, but with clarity, confidence, and collective strength.
